script: Indianapolis is laying 6.5 with a 43.5 total, so the lean is a Colts lead that keeps Jonathan Taylor in a heavy carry role (58 carries, 208 rush yards over weeks 3-5) while Tennessee has to throw. That 43.5 total is not a shootout, but a second-half deficit still pushes Cam Ward dropbacks toward Carnell Tate (26 targets, 375 air yards) more than Tony Pollard (47 carries, 174 rush yards).
who_goes_off: Carnell Tate is the TEN piece who should go off: 209 receiving yards on 26 targets over the last three games, a 69.7-yard average against a 50.0 line, with IND allowing 8.72 YPA in the middle and 8.29 to the left. Jonathan Taylor gets the touches (19.3 carries per game) but Tennessee's 3.78 YPC allowed caps the efficiency spike Indianapolis's 5.21 YPC run defense would otherwise give a back.
weak_spot: IND's real leak is the run (5.21 YPC, 14 runs of 10+) and the middle of the field (8.72 YPA on 36 attempts), not the right side (7.60 YPA on 75 attempts), plus 16 passes of 20+ on 176 attempts. TEN's defense is the opposite shape: 3.78 YPC allowed and a flat pass map (left 8.02 on 49 attempts, middle 8.03 on 32, right 7.58 on 65), with 15 passes of 20+ on 156 attempts.
injury_fallout: No injury report was saved for TEN@IND, so the usage read is weeks 3-5: Carnell Tate and Wan'Dale Robinson (23 targets, 129 yards) own the TEN pass game while Calvin Ridley is down to 6 targets and 46 yards, and IND funnels through Tyler Warren (24 targets, 179 yards) and Jonathan Taylor rather than Daniel Jones as a runner (8 carries, 14 yards).
qb_vs_blitz: Cam Ward is the blitz splitter at 0.03 EPA/dropback vs blitz (n=37) and -0.23 with no blitz, but Indianapolis blitzes only 20%, so he mostly sees the look he is losing. Daniel Jones is negative either way (-0.11 vs blitz on 60 dropbacks, -0.18 with no blitz) and Tennessee blitzes just 22%, so neither QB is a blitz-beater in this game.

picks.why: Carnell Tate has 209 yards on 26 targets over three games (69.7 per game) against a 50.0 line, with 375 air yards, and IND allows 8.72 YPA in the middle plus 16 explosives of 20+; a TEN trail behind the 6.5 spread adds the dropbacks his target share already wins.

Jonathan Taylor is at 208 rush yards on 58 carries (69.3 per game, 3.59 YPC) against an 89.5 line, and TEN allows only 3.78 YPC; even 20 carries at that rate is about 76 yards, so the Colts' -6.5 run script does not clear a number 20 yards above his weeks 3-5 average.
